result.title: From Glance to Focus: Mitigating Recognition Laziness in MLLMs for Fine-Grained Recognition
result.comment: 21 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables. Includes supplementary material
result.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) generally fall short of expectations in Fine-Grained Visual Recognition (FGVR), although they exhibit promising FGVR foundations, i.e., visual perception and broad category knowledge. Most existing studies seek to remedy this deficiency by adopting domain-specific post-training, at the risk of compromising generalization to unseen domains. Different from these efforts, in this paper, we revisit the FGVR mechanism underlying MLLMs from both the empirical and theoretical perspectives and uncover an inference-time phenomenon termed FGVR Laziness. In brief, FGVR Laziness refers to the insufficient association between visual cues and category concepts under certain candidate category lists and recognition guidance, leaving the FGVR foundations of MLLMs largely under-utilized. To mitigate FGVR Laziness, we propose Laziness-resIstant Visual rEcognition (LIVE), a training-free framework which jointly refines candidate lists and recognition guidance to elicit the latent FGVR capability of MLLMs. Specifically, LIVE first performs query-adaptive candidate inference to derive a compact yet reliable candidate list. Meanwhile, LIVE constructs category-specific FGVR skills by mining the intra-category characteristics and inter-category differences. Finally, LIVE selectively invokes detailed skill guidance according to recognition uncertainty and category confusion, shifting MLLM-based FGVR from a cursory glance to a focus on associating discriminative visual cues with category concepts. Extensive experiments on 13 benchmarks against 24 state-of-the-art methods spanning fine-grained category recognition, action recognition, and general category recognition, verify the effectiveness and generalizability of LIVE across different MLLM backbones. The code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从实证与理论两方面重新审视 MLLM 做细粒度视觉识别（FGVR）的内在机制，指出推理期存在「FGVR Laziness」现象，即视觉线索与类别概念关联不足，并提出免训练的 LIVE 框架：查询自适应地压缩候选类别列表，并依据识别不确定性与类别混淆，选择性调用由类内特征与类间差异构建的技能指导。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心诊断「视觉线索与类别概念关联不足、潜在 FGVR 能力未被利用」对应视觉细节保留与视觉旁路、信息坍缩问题；按不确定性/混淆度选择性触发详细指导，可供核查 THINK/LOOK/STOP 类动态证据获取与停止决策的收益与成本。
